question: Refer to the exhibit. Which command is run from the Guest Shell to set the description on the first five interfaces of the Cisco Nexus switch?
context:
interface Ethernet1/1
  description Server1
interface Ethernet1/2
  description Server2
interface Ethernet1/3
  description Server3
interface Ethernet1/4
  description Server4
interface Ethernet1/5
  description Server5
options: [guestshell@guestshell ~]$ for x in (1..5); dohost "conf t ; interface eth1/$x ; description Server$x"
[guestshell@guestshell ~]$ for x in (1..5); do dohost "conf t ; interface eth1/$x ; description Server$x"; done
[guestshell@guestshell ~]$ for x in (1..5); do dohost "conf t3_x\ninterface eth1/$x1_x\ndescription Server$x\x€; done
[guestshell@guestshell ~]$ dohost "conf t ; interface eth1/$x ; description Server$x"
theory: A correct Bash for-loop must use the 'do ... done' block syntax, not just a semicolon, so 'for x in (1..5); do dohost "..."; done' is properly formed shell script. Inside the loop body, $x is substituted into the quoted dohost string on each iteration, letting a single loop generate five separate 'interface eth1/$x' / 'description Server$x' NX-OS configuration commands issued through dohost. Options missing 'do'/'done' or omitting the loop entirely are invalid Bash and would either error or only run once. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 16 — Automation and Scripting Tools)
